purpose: Replacement concepts emphasizing analog rock after first set was rejected as next-gen

concepts.title: Garage
concepts.direction: GARAGE ROCK / 1970s TWO-INK CONCERT SCREENPRINT. Dominant warm aged cream paper, charcoal ink and bold burnt orange-red. Huge heavy rounded slab-serif QUADER logotype, imperfect ink edges, a confident blocky Projects subtitle. A few thick screenprinted horizontal bars, slightly offset orange shadow only behind the brand lettering. The project list resembles a printed record tracklist or setlist: rows are broad alternating cream and warm orange bands, project titles large dark slab-serif, metadata small clear black typewriter-like text. Selected first row is solid charcoal with warm cream lettering. Open/New are blunt solid ink rectangles in the header, no outlines or gradients. The two resource areas are compact liner-note-like strips at the bottom with highly reduced two-ink architecture illustrations. Material: genuine rough paper fiber and inconsistent screenprint coverage in open areas only. Loud warm human analog character. The whole screenshot should be overwhelmingly cream/rust, radically different from a black tech dashboard. No invented slogans, band names or literal instruments.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a single full-frame landscape desktop UI design mockup for QUADER, a professional 3D level-design app, showing its project list. This is a NEW art direction from scratch, not a reskin of a standard tech dashboard. The user rejected sleek metal, chamfers, thin purple outlines, futuristic wide type and polished sci-fi panels. They want actual ROCK MUSIC visual culture: analog, visceral, tactile, art-directed, rebellious. The interface should have the soul of the specified rock print genre, while remaining readable and usable.
Image is the actual flat application screen, front-on, landscape approximately 16:10. No computer or phone mockup, no perspective, desk, guitars or stage in an environment, no external annotation. Intentionally strong editorial design, very high visual craft, texture controlled to avoid damaging body text.
Functional content only: brand text "QUADER"; heading "Projects"; main actions "Open project…" and "New project"; heading "Recent projects". Four selectable project rows, with aligned metadata columns labeled "Last modified" and "Editor version", a secondary file path under each project name, and an overflow ellipsis at row end:
"Courtyard" / "C:/Projects/Courtyard/Courtyard.qproj" / "2 hours ago" / "v0.1.42";
"Industrial passage" / "C:/Projects/Industrial passage/Industrial passage.qproj" / "Yesterday" / "v0.1.42";
"Lighting studies" / "C:/Projects/Lighting studies/Lighting studies.qproj" / "3 days ago" / "v0.1.41";
"Archived prototype" / "D:/Archive/Prototype/Prototype.qproj" / "Unavailable" / "—".
First row selected; last row muted. Preserve clear readable names and metadata. Dense but comfortable project list; not a gallery.
Two secondary resource areas: "Your first hour in Quader" / "Start tutorial", with a small greybox staircase scene; "Read the Docs" / "Open docs", with small isometric block architecture. These illustrations must be treated in the chosen print aesthetic. No added slogans, fake features, new controls, tags, accounts or data.
Rock character must be obvious from the composition, palette, mark-making, display typography and materials, not dependent on literal music props. Use a normal clear readable face for path/date/version/control text. A tiny purple Q brand mark may remain, but the palette should follow the chosen direction, not purple tech UI.
Strictly avoid: futuristic visual language, gaming launcher, sci-fi HUD, neon glow, bevelled chrome, brushed metal, chamfered frames, spaceship panels, thin luminous accent outlines, widely tracked techno lettering, glassmorphism, gradients, SaaS cards, generic dark-mode design, modern polished luxury mood. No added words beyond functional labels listed.

concepts.title: Grunge
concepts.direction: 1990s GRUNGE ALBUM SLEEVE / REHEARSAL-ROOM NOTICEBOARD. Dominant dirty charcoal, faded olive, warm gray and muted rust, with scraps of ivory masking tape. A large rough brush-lettered but legible QUADER brand at top left, offset, imperfect, hand-painted rather than techno. Heading Projects is a simple worn white stencil. Several long torn strips of pale paper form one coherent vertical project manifest against a dark fibrous field; DO NOT use floating rounded cards. The selected first project row sits on a long cream masking-tape strip with dark text and a black marker bar in the number gutter. Other rows are printed directly on the dark surface in warm off-white, split only by rough thin horizontal strokes; crisp small gray metadata. A little authentic photocopy texture, staple-sized marks at margins, scratches and faded ink in unused corners, while text is sharp. New/Open are plain block buttons resembling black ink stamps on light tape, generous click targets. Two resource areas arranged at the bottom like rough album liner-note inserts with grainy black-and-white architectural photos. Rugged tactile worn-in handmade identity, quietly angry rather than futuristic. No metallic hardware, neon, grids of tiny technical labels, or clean laser-cut panels.

concepts.title: Punk
concepts.direction: 1977 PUNK PHOTOCOPIED GIG FLYER / DIY FANZINE. Forceful black, dirty white and saturated vermilion red, almost no gray. Large tight condensed black QUADER wordmark on a torn white header strip; a deliberately tilted red paper rectangle under the clear Projects heading. A punchy asymmetric composition: project list takes roughly the left three quarters of the screen, while the two tutorial/docs resource blocks are stacked in a narrow right rail as photocopied architectural flyer fragments, clearly usable. Main actions Open project… and New project are high-contrast stamped rectangular buttons in the top action band. Project rows resemble a gig lineup: gigantic row numbers in the narrow left margin, bold names, tiny perfectly aligned metadata, generous vertical gaps. Selected row has a thick red marker swipe behind its name with high-contrast white text and a red stroke along the left; no rounded card boundary. Halftone, torn-edge paper, coarse photocopy noise only in header, separators, and small illustrations. DIY pasted typography with deliberate baseline tension, but no collisions and no text fragmentation. Should look unmistakably punk and provocative at first glance. No slogans, stickers with words, band names or safety pins over controls. No sleek metal or fine futuristic geometry.

concepts.title: Doom
concepts.direction: UNDERGROUND HEAVY-METAL VINYL SLEEVE / DOOM ROCK PRINT. Faded ink black, warm bone-white and a single muted oxblood-red selection band. One bold, readable, aggressive gothic-serif QUADER wordmark, much larger than ordinary app branding, with rough woodcut edge treatment; the small Projects heading below remains clean. Sparse worn ink margins and engraved architectural motifs restricted to the header ends and two footer images. Project names use an assertive heavy old-style serif, metadata and action labels use a plain highly legible sans serif. Centered wide dense project manifest, four rows separated by substantial uneven ivory print rules; selected Courtyard row is a deep oxblood horizontal band with bone-white text, the other rows charcoal-black. Open/New at upper right are square flat ivory/oxblood buttons, no medieval button ornaments. Footer resource areas rework the staircase and isometric block geometry as severe etched/woodcut album artwork. Old record-sleeve darkness and weight, analog, serious, unforgettable. Avoid fantasy RPG menu, game launcher, occult symbols, horror/gore, skulls, flames, spikes, ornamental metal frames, chrome, neon, runes, extra words. It should read as rock graphic design for a practical creative tool.
